scenarios.title: A creature assigns combat damage equal to its power, and none when its power is 0

setup.notes: All creatures have been under their controllers' control since before this turn. Giant Growth is used only in the pumped_power variant.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B blocks Grizzly Bears with Hill Giant.
No spells or abilities are used; both players pass through the declare blockers step and combat damage is assigned and dealt.

variants.label: equal_to_power
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears assigns 2 damage to Hill Giant and Hill Giant assigns 3 damage to Grizzly Bears. Grizzly Bears (2/2) moves to A's graveyard; Hill Giant (3/3) stays on the battlefield with 2 damage marked.

variants.label: zero_power_blocker
variants.delta: B blocks Grizzly Bears with Wall of Wood (0/3) instead of Hill Giant.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears assigns 2 damage to Wall of Wood; Wall of Wood has power 0 and assigns no combat damage at all. Grizzly Bears has no damage marked and stays on the battlefield, and Wall of Wood survives with 2 damage marked.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B blocks Grizzly Bears with Wall of Wood (0/3) instead of Hill Giant

variants.label: pumped_power
variants.delta: In the declare blockers step, after the block, A casts Giant Growth (tapping Forest) targeting Grizzly Bears and it resolves.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears has power 5 and assigns 5 damage to Hill Giant, which moves to B's graveyard; Hill Giant assigns 3 damage to Grizzly Bears (5/5 until end of turn), which survives with 3 damage marked.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: In the declare blockers step, after the block, A casts Giant Growth (tapping Forest) targeting Grizzly Bears and it resolves

detector.outcome: Each creature in combat deals combat damage equal to its power: the combat record holds combat damage_dealt events.
detector.near_miss: A creature in combat with power 0 or less deals no combat damage (no near miss is counted without an api).

scenarios.title: An unblocked attacker assigns its damage to what it attacks, and none if it attacks nothing

setup.notes: Jace Beleren has 3 loyalty counters. Grizzly Bears has been under A's control since before this turn. B controls no creatures. Lightning Bolt is used only in the walker_removed variant.

decisions: A attacks Jace Beleren with Grizzly Bears.
B declares no blockers.
No spells or abilities are used; both players pass and combat damage is assigned and dealt.

variants.label: attack_planeswalker
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is unblocked and assigns its 2 damage to Jace Beleren, which loses 2 loyalty counters and stays on the battlefield with 1. B's life stays 20.

variants.label: attack_player
variants.delta: A attacks B (the player) with Grizzly Bears instead of Jace Beleren.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is unblocked and assigns its 2 damage to B, whose life becomes 18. Jace Beleren keeps 3 loyalty counters.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A attacks B (the player) with Grizzly Bears instead of Jace Beleren

variants.label: walker_removed
variants.delta: After no blockers are declared, A casts Lightning Bolt (tapping Mountain) targeting Jace Beleren and it resolves before combat damage.
variants.expected: Jace Beleren takes 3 damage, loses all its loyalty and moves to B's graveyard. Grizzly Bears remains in combat attacking nothing and assigns no combat damage: B's life stays 20.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: After no blockers are declared, A casts Lightning Bolt (tapping Mountain) targeting Jace Beleren and it resolves before combat damage

scenarios.forge_notes: When the attacked planeswalker leaves, Forge keeps the attacker in combat attacking a placeholder defender and assigns its damage there, not to the player: Forge follows the rule.

detector.outcome: An unblocked attacker's combat damage goes to the player, planeswalker or battle it attacks: a combat damage_dealt event whose subject is not attacking or blocking.
detector.near_miss: Every combat damage event of the step goes to a creature in combat, as when the attackers were blocked.

scenarios.title: A blocked attacker assigns damage to its blockers, and none if no blockers remain

setup.notes: All creatures have been under their controllers' control since before this turn. Lightning Bolt is used only in the blocker_removed variant.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B blocks Grizzly Bears with Hill Giant only.
No spells or abilities are used; both players pass and combat damage is assigned and dealt.

variants.label: single_blocker
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears assigns all 2 of its damage to Hill Giant, which stays on the battlefield with 2 damage marked; Hill Giant assigns 3 damage to Grizzly Bears, which moves to A's graveyard. B's life stays 20.

variants.label: blocker_removed
variants.delta: After the block, A casts Lightning Bolt (tapping Mountain) targeting Hill Giant and it resolves.
variants.expected: Hill Giant moves to B's graveyard before damage. Grizzly Bears stays blocked but no creature is blocking it, so it assigns no combat damage; B's life stays 20, Wall of Wood has no damage and Grizzly Bears survives undamaged.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: After the block, A casts Lightning Bolt (tapping Mountain) targeting Hill Giant and it resolves

variants.label: two_blockers
variants.delta: B blocks Grizzly Bears with both Hill Giant and Wall of Wood, and A divides its damage 1 to Hill Giant and 1 to Wall of Wood.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears assigns 1 damage to Hill Giant and 1 to Wall of Wood, which both survive with 1 damage marked. Hill Giant assigns 3 damage to Grizzly Bears, which moves to A's graveyard; Wall of Wood assigns none.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B blocks Grizzly Bears with both Hill Giant and Wall of Wood, and A divides its damage 1 to Hill Giant and 1 to Wall of Wood

detector.outcome: A blocked attacker's combat damage is dealt to the creatures blocking it: a combat damage_dealt event whose subject is a creature in combat.
detector.near_miss: Combat damage in the step goes only to what is not in combat (an unblocked attacker's damage to the player, planeswalker or battle it attacks).

scenarios.title: A blocking creature assigns damage to what it blocks, and none if it blocks nothing

setup.notes: Call A's creatures Bears 1 and Bears 2. All creatures have been under their controllers' control since before this turn. Noble Ox (2/4) can block any number of creatures. Shock is used only in the attacker_removed variant.

decisions: A attacks B with Bears 1 only.
B blocks Bears 1 with Noble Ox.
No spells or abilities are used; both players pass and combat damage is assigned and dealt.

variants.label: single_blocked
variants.expected: Noble Ox assigns all 2 of its damage to Bears 1, which moves to A's graveyard; Bears 1 assigns 2 damage to Noble Ox, which stays on the battlefield (2/4) with 2 damage marked.

variants.label: attacker_removed
variants.delta: After the block, B casts Shock (tapping Mountain) targeting Bears 1 and it resolves.
variants.expected: Bears 1 moves to A's graveyard before damage. Noble Ox is blocking nothing, so it assigns no combat damage; it has no damage marked and A's Bears 2 is untouched.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: After the block, B casts Shock (tapping Mountain) targeting Bears 1 and it resolves

variants.label: two_blocked
variants.delta: A attacks with both Bears 1 and Bears 2, Noble Ox blocks both, and B divides its damage 1 to each.
variants.expected: Noble Ox assigns 1 damage to each Bears, which both survive with 1 damage marked; Bears 1 and Bears 2 together assign 4 damage to Noble Ox, which moves to B's graveyard.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A attacks with both Bears 1 and Bears 2, Noble Ox blocks both, and B divides its damage 1 to each

detector.outcome: A blocking creature's combat damage is dealt to the attacker it blocks: a combat damage_dealt event whose subject is a creature in combat.
detector.near_miss: Combat damage in the step goes only to what is not in combat, no blocker dealing damage to an attacker.

scenarios.title: Combat damage is dealt simultaneously, so a creature that dies still deals its damage

setup.notes: All creatures have been under their controllers' control since before this turn. Youthful Knight (2/1) has first strike.

decisions: A attacks B with its Grizzly Bears.
B blocks with its Grizzly Bears (base variant).
No spells or abilities are used; both players pass and combat damage is assigned and dealt.

variants.label: simultaneous
variants.expected: Both Grizzly Bears assign 2 damage in the same combat damage step, and both are dealt at once: both creatures have lethal damage and move to their owners' graveyards.

variants.label: first_strike_blocker
variants.delta: B blocks with Youthful Knight (first strike) instead of its Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: The damage is not simultaneous: in the first combat damage step Youthful Knight deals 2 damage and A's Grizzly Bears moves to A's graveyard before it can deal damage. Youthful Knight has no damage marked and stays on the battlefield.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B blocks with Youthful Knight (first strike) instead of its Grizzly Bears

detector.outcome: Combat damage is dealt simultaneously: several creatures deal combat damage in one damage step, those the state-based check then kills included.
detector.near_miss: A combat damage step in which fewer than two damage events happen.

scenarios.title: A trigger on combat damage is put on the stack before the active player gets priority

setup.notes: Slith Firewalker (1/1 haste): whenever it deals combat damage to a player, put a +1/+1 counter on it. All creatures have been under their controllers' control since before this turn.

decisions: A attacks B with Slith Firewalker.
B declares no blockers (base variant).
No spells or abilities are used until the combat damage step; when A first receives priority there, A passes and then B passes.

variants.label: unblocked
variants.expected: Slith Firewalker deals 1 combat damage to B (life 19). Its trigger fires and is already on the stack when A first gets priority in the combat damage step; when it resolves Slith Firewalker has a +1/+1 counter and is 2/2.

variants.label: blocked
variants.delta: B blocks Slith Firewalker with Wall of Wood.
variants.expected: Slith Firewalker deals its 1 damage to Wall of Wood, not to a player: the trigger does not fire, nothing is on the stack when A gets priority, B stays at 20 life and Slith Firewalker stays 1/1.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B blocks Slith Firewalker with Wall of Wood

detector.outcome: A 'deals damage' trigger fires on the damage dealt, combat damage among it.
detector.near_miss: The trigger is evaluated and does not fire because the damage was not dealt to the kind of recipient it names.

scenarios.title: A trigger on a state-based death after combat damage is put on the stack before the active player gets priority

setup.notes: Zulaport Cutthroat (1/1) stays home: whenever it or another creature A controls dies, each opponent loses 1 life and A gains 1 life. All creatures have been under their controllers' control since before this turn.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears only.
B blocks Grizzly Bears with Hill Giant (base variant).
No spells or abilities are used until the combat damage step; when A first receives priority there, A passes and then B passes.

variants.label: attacker_dies
variants.expected: Hill Giant deals 3 to Grizzly Bears, which dies in the state-based check right after damage. Zulaport Cutthroat's trigger is already on the stack when A first gets priority in the combat damage step; when it resolves B is at 19 and A at 21.

variants.label: attacker_survives
variants.delta: B blocks Grizzly Bears with Wall of Wood instead of Hill Giant.
variants.expected: Wall of Wood deals no damage, Grizzly Bears survives, Zulaport Cutthroat does not trigger and the stack is empty when A gets priority; both players stay at 20 life.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B blocks Grizzly Bears with Wall of Wood instead of Hill Giant

detector.outcome: A creature-dies trigger is evaluated and fires in the combat damage step, after the state-based check put a creature into the graveyard.
detector.near_miss: The same kind of trigger is evaluated in the combat damage step and does not fire (no creature died).

scenarios.title: A first strike or double strike creature in combat splits combat damage into two steps

setup.notes: All creatures have been under their controllers' control since before this turn. Youthful Knight (2/1) has first strike; Fencing Ace (1/1) has double strike.

decisions: A attacks B with A's Grizzly Bears only.
B blocks with Youthful Knight (base variant).
No spells or abilities are used; both players pass through every combat damage step.

variants.label: first_strike_blocker
variants.expected: In the first combat damage step only Youthful Knight deals damage: 2 to Grizzly Bears, which moves to A's graveyard. In the second combat damage step Grizzly Bears is gone and deals no damage; Youthful Knight has no damage marked and survives.

variants.label: no_first_strike
variants.delta: B blocks with its Grizzly Bears instead of Youthful Knight.
variants.expected: There is no first strike or double strike creature in combat, so there is a single combat damage step in which both Grizzly Bears deal 2 damage at once and both move to their owners' graveyards.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B blocks with its Grizzly Bears instead of Youthful Knight

variants.label: survives_first_strike
variants.delta: A attacks with Hill Giant instead of Grizzly Bears, and Youthful Knight blocks it.
variants.expected: In the first step Youthful Knight deals 2 damage to Hill Giant (3/3), which survives. In the second step Hill Giant deals 3 damage to Youthful Knight, which moves to B's graveyard; Youthful Knight, with first strike only, deals no damage in the second step. Hill Giant stays with 2 damage marked.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A attacks with Hill Giant instead of Grizzly Bears, and Youthful Knight blocks it

variants.label: double_strike_blocker
variants.delta: B blocks Grizzly Bears with Fencing Ace instead of Youthful Knight.
variants.expected: In the first step Fencing Ace deals 1 damage to Grizzly Bears, which survives with 1 damage. In the second step Fencing Ace deals 1 more and Grizzly Bears deals 2 damage to it: Grizzly Bears (2 damage in total) and Fencing Ace both move to their owners' graveyards.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B blocks Grizzly Bears with Fencing Ace instead of Youthful Knight

detector.outcome: A real combat in which a creature with first strike deals damage, so combat damage is dealt in a separate first-strike step.
detector.near_miss: A damage-step probe fork that re-ran the combat with first strike stripped from its carrier.
